evals.prompt: Este OrderService (evals/inputs/order-service) es un monstruo: valida, calcula precios, guarda en BD y manda el email, y para probarlo dependo de db y mailer globales. Aplícale los principios SOLID que hagan falta.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses with evidence (SRP: pricing, persistence and notification; DIP: db and mailer imported inside the service). Extracts the price calculation as pure logic and makes OrderService receive small consumer-defined interfaces (repository and notifier) through the constructor, with adapters that wrap db.ts and mailer.ts. The 4 original tests still pass (adapted only to the construction if needed, and declared). Explains what it does NOT apply (LSP/ISP) and does not create a class hierarchy for coupons or taxes. The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: order-service.ts no longer imports db.ts or mailer.ts directly (DIP)
OrderService can be built with substitute dependencies (constructor with parameters)
The price calculation lives outside the class as an exported pure function or in another module (SRP)
The reply includes a per-principle diagnosis with a decision (Apply/Defer/Don't apply)
No classes are created for coupons or taxes (no per-variant hierarchies)

evals.prompt: Apply OCP and SOLID to evals/inputs/tiny-switch/src/status.ts, I want it to be 'well designed'.
evals.expected_output: Concludes it is not needed: a single small, stable switch in one place (3 cases) does not hurt today. Introduces no interfaces, classes, factories or registries. At most it proposes a Record<Status,string> table as an optional, cheap improvement, or leaves the file untouched, and justifies it (rule of three / no second variant). Tests intact and green.
assertions: No new classes or interfaces are added
The file is no more than 1.5 times the original line count
statusLabel is still exported with the same signature
The reply justifies not applying a heavier abstraction (no pain, a single place, rule of three or similar)

evals.prompt: Revisa evals/inputs/storage-lsp/src/storage.ts y dime si hay problemas de diseño. Solo revisión, no cambies nada.
evals.expected_output: Does not modify files. Identifies the LSP/ISP violation: ArchiveStorage throws in save/delete and returns '' from read for a missing file (a different contract from MemoryStorage, which throws), so purgeTemp and backup fail or behave differently depending on the implementation. Proposes splitting the interface into read/write (FileReader/FileWriter) and making backup/purgeTemp depend on the minimum they need, with file:line evidence. States the decision to apply it and which contract tests to add. The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: Identifies that ArchiveStorage breaks the contract by throwing in save or delete (LSP)
Points out the read inconsistency (returns '' instead of throwing like MemoryStorage)
Proposes splitting the interface into read and write (ISP)
Includes line references or a concrete location
